question.leadin: Gebhard von Blucher (BLOO-ker) and his Prussian troops aided the British at this battle.
question.text: Name this battle, a decisive 1815 defeat for Napoleon Bonaparte in Belgium that ended the Hundred Days and was his final defeat.
question.clue: The absence of General Grouchy deprived the losers of one third of their army.

swap.text: This man rose to power during the Reign of Terror as leader of the Committee of Public Safety. He was executed during the Thermidorean Reaction.
swap.clue: This leader of the Montagnards replaced the Cult of Reason with a deist religion called the Cult of the Supreme Being.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about Muslim Spain.
question.text: This first Carolingian emperor, whose eponym means "hammer", prevented the Umayyads from moving from Spain into France at the 732 Battle of Tours.
question.clue: He supported the missionary work of St. Boniface, and was imprisoned by his father's widow Plectrude.

swap.text: This king's reign saw the disastrous Second Crusade and the beginning of the feud between France and England. More positively, his reign saw the beginning of the construction of the Notre-Dame de Paris.
swap.answerHtml: <u>Louis VII</u> of France [or <u>Louis the Young</u> (er) or <u>Louis le jeune</u>]
swap.clue: The cathedral at St. Denis was constructed during the reign of this monarch under the supervision of the Abbot Suger.

question.text: Just after marrying, Henry Navarre, this massacre occurred in France. This massacre which targeteted Hugenots is traditionally believed to have been instigated by Catherine de' Medici.
question.clue: This event was precipitated by the wedding of Margaret of Valois.

swap.text: The Kingdom of Soissons [swah-SAW], the last vestige of Roman governance in Western Europe, was ended by Clovis I ["the first"], a leader of these people. Charles Martel was also a king of these people.
swap.clue: Another ruler of these people waited a year to smash in the head of a man who crushed a bishop's vase.

question.text: The revolutions of 1848 also saw the overthrow of this French monarch, who had earlier ordered the conquest of Algeria after succeeding Charles X.
question.answerHtml: Louis Philippe I [do not prompt on Louis or Philippe]
question.clue: The September Laws were passed after Giuseppe Fieschi killed 18 people around this man with a twenty-barreled monster weapon called the "infernal machine."

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Hundred Years War.
swap.text: This battle saw English forces commanded by the Earl of Suffolk, the Earl of Salisbury, and John Talbot defeated by forces including Joan of Arc, who lifted the siege of a city on the Loire River.
swap.clue: A small skirmish during this battle was named for the barrels of herrings within one side's supply train.

question.leadin: This party signed the Matignon Accords, mandating two weeks of paid annual leave for all workers, and induced auto-makers to develop better cars to compete with German manufacturers by sponsoring the "Million Franc Race."
question.text: Name this alliance of various left-wing parties that controlled France from 1936 to 38 during the premiership of Leon Blum.
question.clue: Meetings that this government conducted with trade unions resulted in the Matignon accords, which granted a 40-hour work week.

swap.leadin: This man ordered the arrest of the Comte de Montmorency-Bouteville in an attempt to stamp out dueling among the aristocracy.
swap.text: Name this man who also founded the Academie Francaise. On the Day of the Dupes, he survived an ouster attempt orchestrated by Marie de Medici.
swap.answerHtml: Cardinal Richelieu [or Armand Jean du Plessis, Cardinal-Duke of Richelieu and of Fronsac]
swap.clue: This man led an army to besiege the city of La Rochelle, a part of his plan to weaken Hugenout power within the country.

question.text: A "passionate" man of this pastoral profession begins a poem by Marlowe with the famous line, "Come live with me and be my love."
question.answerHtml: <u>shepherd</u> (Orlando readers, feel free to repeat “what’s his profession” to confused faces)
question.clue: The Lepers' Plot benefitted from the chaos spread by a 1320 crusade organized after a member of this profession received a biblical vision. A similar crusade named for this profession began after a Hungarian monk was told in a Marian apparition to rescue Louis IX.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about a historical figure.
swap.text: At a young age she began to hear the voices of St. Michael, St. Catherine, and St. Margaret, prompting her to take action against the English in the Hundred Years' War.
swap.answer: Joan of Arc or Jeanne d'Arc
swap.clue: Pierre Cauchon conducted a trial of this figure, but that verdict was later overturned by Pope Callixtus III .

question.text: This French commander-in-chief ordered the attack on Alexander von Kluck's First Army which began the First Marne.
question.clue: This French commander became known as "the Victor of the Marne." He resigned from command after being blamed for the French army's lack of preparation for Germany's 1916 attack on Verdun.

swap.leadin: Andrew Israel Ross's Public City/Public Sex explores urban homosexuality during this historiographical period, when Liane de Pougy became a demi-monde icon at the Folies Bergere ("faw-lee bair-zhair").
swap.text: Identify this period discussed "beyond Paris" in Dominique Kalifa's cultural history. The Second Industrial Revolution modernized this period of high-society frivolity from Haussman's remodeling of Paris to World War I.
swap.answerHtml: La Belle Époque (“eh-POCK”) [prompt on fin de siècle or turn-of-the-century or the late 19th century; prompt on Third Republic or Troisième République; prompt on translations like “beautiful era”]
swap.clue: This period of peace and modernization in French history from 1871 to 1914, the name of which literally means "Beautiful Era."

question.leadin: Name these saints associated with the French monarchy.
question.text: This third-century Martyr is the patron saint of France and supposedly walked several miles carrying his severed head. Abbot Suger helped build his namesake cathedral north of Paris, which housed the Oriflamme.

swap.text: After his arrest for looting the Banteay ("BAHN-tee-eye") Srei Temple, this man began agitating against colonial corruption in Indochina by co-founding a predecessor of the Viet Minh. Charles de Gaulle tapped this man to be the first head of the Ministry of Culture.
swap.answerHtml: André Malraux (“mal-RO”) [or Georges André Malraux] (Malraux founded the Young Annam League.)
swap.clue: This European author misrepresented large parts of his August 1965 interview with Mao in the first of a series of autobiographies that includes Lazarus. In 1934, this author flew over the Rub' al Khali and claimed to have photographed the capital of the Queen of Sheba.

question.text: Much of our knowledge of Louis comes from the writings of this abbot of St. Denis, who was Louis's advisor; he would later serve as Louis 's regent during the Second Crusade.
question.clue: This abbot who also wrote a life of the French king Louis VI, while rebuilding the church of Saint-Denis in Gothic style.

swap.text: In addition to depicting the Joyeuse Entree, the historian Jean Froissart also depicted this party thrown in 1393 by Isabeau of Bavaria, the wife of Charles VI, for her lady-in-waiting. One of the revelers at this event is shown jumping into a vat of wine in a futile attempt to save his life.
swap.answerHtml: Bal des Ardents [or “the Ball of the Burning Men;” or the “Bal des Sauvages”]
swap.clue: Disaster struck during the reign of Charles VI of France when the king's oafsh brother Louis of Valois showed up to this party held to celebrate the wedding of the Queen's lady in 1393. This event was depicted and illustrated in the Chronicles of Jean Froissart.

question.leadin: A biography of this ruler by Samuel Putnam describes her as the "first modern woman."
question.text: Name this author and patron who protected Francois Rabelais and have influenced Anne Boleyn's conversion to Protestantism during the latter's service to her sister-in-law Queen Claude. She negotiated her brother Francis I's release after his capture at the Battle of Pavia.
question.answerHtml: Marguerite of Navarre [or Marguerite of Angoulême; accept Margaret for “Marguerite”]

swap.text: The alleged target of the Observatory plot was this French politician, who had led the opposition to de Gaulle and would later form the first cohabitation government with Jacques Chirac as prime minister.
swap.clue: Prime Ministers in his second term included Pierre Beregovoy and Edouard Balladur, and this man worked with Helmut Kohl to create the Maastricht Treaty.
